title: Security & Access Control
painPoint: Security and access control systems rely on magnetic components for electromagnetic locking, door positioning, and tamper detection. Maglocks require high holding-force N42 and N48 magnets that maintain grip under vibration and temperature swings from -20°C to 60°C. Access control reed sensors demand compact magnets with stable flux over years of continuous use, yet standard grades suffer corrosion in humid entrance environments and flux drift at temperature extremes. Engineers need NdFeB magnets offering high pull-force in minimal volume, consistent flux for reliable sensor triggering, and coatings that withstand condensation, cleaning chemicals, and UV exposure in both indoor and outdoor perimeter security installations.
